{
  "reviews": [
    {
      "actor": "lin",
      "decision": "develop",
      "ability": null,
      "reason": "No implemented capability supplies a persistent, fuel-consuming local heat source compatible with ordinary rest. Exercise spends energy continuously; shelter and a mantle reduce cooling but do not produce heat. Branches are a plausible fuel input, but Lin currently owns neither fuel nor ignition equipment. Develop material preparation, friction ignition and tending together. Rain, wind, moisture and placement must affect actual success and heat delivery; development supplies no materials, fire or mastery.",
      "specification": "Implement revision local-fire@1 through the current conversation handoff, with public interface tend-fire and no mastery prerequisites. Learning covers fuel preparation, friction ignition and safe tending; existing gathering, inventory, weather, collision, exposure and rest systems remain dependencies.

Public schema: strict object with mode enum [prepare,build,ignite,feed,extinguish], target string, materials array of {target:string,quantity:number in positive exact tenths}, and optional numeric x,y. Require x,y and materials only for build; target and materials for prepare/feed; target only for ignite/extinguish. Reject inappropriate fields. All references follow shared item:/object:/resource: resolution, exact-ID aliases and ambiguity reporting; resolve identities once. Prepare targets an owned branch stack; other targets are visible fire-site objects. Material inputs must be owned, unreserved instances. No remote interaction or automatic acquisition.

Executable precursor: prepare consumes one branch unit over four stationary rounds at 1 energy/round, producing one persistent friction kit of equal input mass, with ten ignition-attempt durability. Its board and spindle are not fuel while intact. Build consumes four stone units, two bark units and one vine over four stationary rounds at 1.5 energy/round, creating an unlit stone hearth with a raised bark rain cover. Input mass remains in its components. Reserve material once; output exists only at completion. Build center must be within 0.65 of the builder, on traversable non-water ground. A radius-0.45 site plus radius-0.25 clearance must avoid solid objects, actors and doors. Hearth is a shared solid circle; its cover is not a room, walkable roof or insulation service. Require open sky and no roof above the hearth; do not silently add ventilation to existing shelters.

Persist site identity, geometry, components, cover condition initially 80, moisture, ember state, ordered fuel lots, remaining usable energy and ash/residue provenance. Initialize material moisture from actual inputs. Add a weather adapter exposing documented rain and wind intensities in [0,1] from actual weather, not invented local readings. Cover transmits rain fraction 0.2+0.8*(1-condition/80), wears 0.25 per rainy round and reduces wind at the hearth by 25% while intact. No free repair. Exposed materials gain 0.08*rain moisture per round; dry weather removes 0.01*(1+wind), bounded to [0,1]. Covered site inputs use transmitted rain. These rules permit real drying but do not guarantee ignition during this storm.

Feed transfers selected branch, bark, dry-grass or wood inputs into the adjacent site in one round costing 0.5 energy. Preserve actual fuel-property values, quantity, mass, moisture and source identities; disallow nonfuel materials. A lot's maximum usable energy is quantity*fuel-property; moisture reduces burn rate rather than generating energy. Consume fuel fractions deterministically, tracking converted mass as persistent nonfuel ash/residue and released combustion products. Do not treat feeding as ignition. Cap stored combustible mass at 8 and reject excess before payment.

Ignite requires adjacency, one owned friction kit, at least 0.5 dry-grass units and 0.5 branch units already loaded, their moisture <=0.35, transmitted rain <=0.15, and effective wind <=0.65. It takes eight consecutive stationary rounds at 1.5 energy/round. Recheck conditions each round. Spend one kit durability and consume 0.1 dry-grass unit at the first friction stroke; remaining tinder and fuel are burned only by the live process after successful completion. Insufficient energy, invalid weather, movement or death cancels the attempt without creating embers. Worn-out kits remain material objects, not replenished equipment.

A burning hearth consumes up to one usable fuel-energy unit per round, multiplied by max(0,1-moisture), with ordered lot accounting. Lit fuel dries by 0.08 per round before rain wetting. Track embers for at most three rounds without successful combustion; transmitted rain above 0.6 extinguishes immediately. No negative fuel, indefinite embers or generated stock. Extinguish takes one adjacent round and 0.5 energy, dispersing embers without supplying water or refunding consumed fuel; unburned lots remain real site contents. Fire continues independently after the builder leaves or dies, using the same global simulation and budgets.

Heat uses actual shared geometry: for each living actor within distance 2 of the hearth center, with an unobstructed segment to its edge, add 0.6*burnFraction*max(0,1-distance/2)*(1-0.5*wind) body-temperature units per round after ordinary exposure. Walls block heat; do not warm remembered positions or entire rooms. Do not clamp body temperature to comfort: existing overheating and injury remain effective. Apply one heat transfer per source per round, resolving multiple sources through the existing temperature system. Ordinary rest remains available outside the collision footprint and retains its normal recovery. No healing, nutrition, immunity or automatic rest bonus. Public logs report actual fuel burned, heat received and resulting temperature, including cases where temperature still falls.

Execution contract: repeat counts completed operations, not work rounds. Persist operation ID, resolved identities, exact remaining work and per-round payments. Global pauses preserve progress without time advancement. Changing action, lost access, invalid conditions, insufficient energy or death cancels multi-round work. Reserved inventory remains owned by its original owner; release surviving unconsumed escrow exactly once, to inventory if living or the normal death location if dead. Spent effort, consumed tinder and durability remain spent. Successfully transferred site fuel belongs to the persistent site, never to cancelled inventory escrow. No cancellation clones or deletes materials or an already completed hearth.

Declare validated events fire-work-started, fire-work-progress, fire-work-completed, fire-work-cancelled, fire-ignited, fire-fed, fire-burned, fire-extinguished, fire-exposure-measured and fire-comfort-qualified. Include operation/site/actor IDs, material deltas, remaining work and paid effects where applicable. Bind rendering and replay to these events plus persisted snapshots: visible stones and cover, changing fuel pile, embers, flame proportional to combustion, rain attenuation, smoke and cold ash. Smoke is presentation only in this open-air version, explicitly not an invented indoor safety guarantee. Display observed moisture, remaining fuel and measured warmth without revealing unseen resources. Add public memory/task adapters for site references, progress and failure explanations.

Migration is additive: register schemas, handlers, event subscriptions, source-equivalence binding and rendering revision; preserve history, existing inventories, geometry, mastery and protected mental accounts. Existing objects gain no fire or fuel. Implementation, personal learning and subsequent use remain separate; review/development advances no simulation time.",
      "experienceReview": "Measured relief is plausible given Lin's cold discomfort and the recent experience of exercise providing limited warmth. Bind fire-comfort-qualified to the existing thermal-refuge equivalence, not a new alias reward. For each actual recipient, require three consecutive stationary rest/wait rounds with positive measured fire heat, reduced cold discomfort, adequate nutrition and no health loss. Award the existing 1-point, 6-round relief with its shared 12-round cooldown, using maximum rather than addition across shelter, mantle, exercise and fire. Repeated qualifying enjoyment remains eligible. Separately support maintained thermal refuge within that same source: after qualification, each continuing qualifying participation round raises a source-local sustained value by 0.025 to cap 1; other rounds decay it by 0.003 to zero. Re-entry requires three qualifying rounds; the short award retains its cooldown. Combine transient and sustained values by maximum, cap 1, and pass through existing mental accounting without modifying protected balances. Emit measured participation and source changes for replay. No reward for requesting, learning, building, lighting, ownership or merely remaining near an ineffective fire; health and survival remain independent.",
      "visualReview": "The paid effect must be a persistent, spatially located hearth with actual cover, fuel, flame, embers and residue, not a warmth icon attached to Lin. Animation follows recorded combustion and weather; blocked heat and extinguished fires cannot look like active warming. Replay shows construction progress, ignition effort and failure, material payments, fuel depletion, cancellation and actual per-recipient temperature changes. A comfort indicator appears only after the measured event conditions qualify and must not imply safety or healing.",
      "learning": 6
    }
  ]
}

data: {"type":"response.output_text.done","sequence_number":1898,"item_id":"msg_0e44131acce6c77b016b0167e8e69087d18aa64fc9ce4f5098","output_index":1,"content_index":0,"text":"{\n  \"reviews\": [\n    {\n      \"actor\": \"lin\",\n      \"decision\": \"develop\",\n      \"ability\": null,\n      \"reason\": \"No implemented capability supplies a persistent, fuel-consuming local heat source compatible with ordinary rest. Exercise spends energy continuously; shelter and a mantle reduce cooling but do not produce heat. Branches are a plausible fuel input, but Lin currently owns neither fuel nor ignition equipment. Develop material preparation, friction ignition and tending together. Rain, wind, moisture and placement must affect actual success and heat delivery; development supplies no materials, fire or mastery.\",\n      \"specification\": \"Implement revision local-fire@1 through the current conversation handoff, with public interface tend-fire and no mastery prerequisites. Learning covers fuel preparation, friction ignition and safe tending; existing gathering, inventory, weather, collision, exposure and rest systems remain dependencies.\\n\\nPublic schema: strict object with mode enum [prepare,build,ignite,feed,extinguish], target string, materials array of {target:string,quantity:number in positive exact tenths}, and optional numeric x,y. Require x,y and materials only for build; target and materials for prepare/feed; target only for ignite/extinguish. Reject inappropriate fields. All references follow shared item:/object:/resource: resolution, exact-ID aliases and ambiguity reporting; resolve identities once. Prepare targets an owned branch stack; other targets are visible fire-site objects. Material inputs must be owned, unreserved instances. No remote interaction or automatic acquisition.\\n\\nExecutable precursor: prepare consumes one branch unit over four stationary rounds at 1 energy/round, producing one persistent friction kit of equal input mass, with ten ignition-attempt durability. Its board and spindle are not fuel while intact. Build consumes four stone units, two bark units and one vine over four stationary rounds at 1.5 energy/round, creating an unlit stone hearth with a raised bark rain cover. Input mass remains in its components. Reserve material once; output exists only at completion. Build center must be within 0.65 of the builder, on traversable non-water ground. A radius-0.45 site plus radius-0.25 clearance must avoid solid objects, actors and doors. Hearth is a shared solid circle; its cover is not a room, walkable roof or insulation service. Require open sky and no roof above the hearth; do not silently add ventilation to existing shelters.\\n\\nPersist site identity, geometry, components, cover condition initially 80, moisture, ember state, ordered fuel lots, remaining usable energy and ash/residue provenance. Initialize material moisture from actual inputs. Add a weather adapter exposing documented rain and wind intensities in [0,1] from actual weather, not invented local readings. Cover transmits rain fraction 0.2+0.8*(1-condition/80), wears 0.25 per rainy round and reduces wind at the hearth by 25% while intact. No free repair. Exposed materials gain 0.08*rain moisture per round; dry weather removes 0.01*(1+wind), bounded to [0,1]. Covered site inputs use transmitted rain. These rules permit real drying but do not guarantee ignition during this storm.\\n\\nFeed transfers selected branch, bark, dry-grass or wood inputs into the adjacent site in one round costing 0.5 energy. Preserve actual fuel-property values, quantity, mass, moisture and source identities; disallow nonfuel materials. A lot's maximum usable energy is quantity*fuel-property; moisture reduces burn rate rather than generating energy. Consume fuel fractions deterministically, tracking converted mass as persistent nonfuel ash/residue and released combustion products. Do not treat feeding as ignition. Cap stored combustible mass at 8 and reject excess before payment.\\n\\nIgnite requires adjacency, one owned friction kit, at least 0.5 dry-grass units and 0.5 branch units already loaded, their moisture <=0.35, transmitted rain <=0.15, and effective wind <=0.65. It takes eight consecutive stationary rounds at 1.5 energy/round. Recheck conditions each round. Spend one kit durability and consume 0.1 dry-grass unit at the first friction stroke; remaining tinder and fuel are burned only by the live process after successful completion. Insufficient energy, invalid weather, movement or death cancels the attempt without creating embers. Worn-out kits remain material objects, not replenished equipment.\\n\\nA burning hearth consumes up to one usable fuel-energy unit per round, multiplied by max(0,1-moisture), with ordered lot accounting. Lit fuel dries by 0.08 per round before rain wetting. Track embers for at most three rounds without successful combustion; transmitted rain above 0.6 extinguishes immediately. No negative fuel, indefinite embers or generated stock. Extinguish takes one adjacent round and 0.5 energy, dispersing embers without supplying water or refunding consumed fuel; unburned lots remain real site contents. Fire continues independently after the builder leaves or dies, using the same global simulation and budgets.\\n\\nHeat uses actual shared geometry: for each living actor within distance 2 of the hearth center, with an unobstructed segment to its edge, add 0.6*burnFraction*max(0,1-distance/2)*(1-0.5*wind) body-temperature units per round after ordinary exposure. Walls block heat; do not warm remembered positions or entire rooms. Do not clamp body temperature to comfort: existing overheating and injury remain effective. Apply one heat transfer per source per round, resolving multiple sources through the existing temperature system. Ordinary rest remains available outside the collision footprint and retains its normal recovery. No healing, nutrition, immunity or automatic rest bonus. Public logs report actual fuel burned, heat received and resulting temperature, including cases where temperature still falls.\\n\\nExecution contract: repeat counts completed operations, not work rounds. Persist operation ID, resolved identities, exact remaining work and per-round payments. Global pauses preserve progress without time advancement. Changing action, lost access, invalid conditions, insufficient energy or death cancels multi-round work. Reserved inventory remains owned by its original owner; release surviving unconsumed escrow exactly once, to inventory if living or the normal death location if dead. Spent effort, consumed tinder and durability remain spent. Successfully transferred site fuel belongs to the persistent site, never to cancelled inventory escrow. No cancellation clones or deletes materials or an already completed hearth.\\n\\nDeclare validated events fire-work-started, fire-work-progress, fire-work-completed, fire-work-cancelled, fire-ignited, fire-fed, fire-burned, fire-extinguished, fire-exposure-measured and fire-comfort-qualified. Include operation/site/actor IDs, material deltas, remaining work and paid effects where applicable. Bind rendering and replay to these events plus persisted snapshots: visible stones and cover, changing fuel pile, embers, flame proportional to combustion, rain attenuation, smoke and cold ash. Smoke is presentation only in this open-air version, explicitly not an invented indoor safety guarantee. Display observed moisture, remaining fuel and measured warmth without revealing unseen resources. Add public memory/task adapters for site references, progress and failure explanations.\\n\\nMigration is additive: register schemas, handlers, event subscriptions, source-equivalence binding and rendering revision; preserve history, existing inventories, geometry, mastery and protected mental accounts. Existing objects gain no fire or fuel. Implementation, personal learning and subsequent use remain separate; review/development advances no simulation time.\",\n      \"experienceReview\": \"Measured relief is plausible given Lin's cold discomfort and the recent experience of exercise providing limited warmth. Bind fire-comfort-qualified to the existing thermal-refuge equivalence, not a new alias reward. For each actual recipient, require three consecutive stationary rest/wait rounds with positive measured fire heat, reduced cold discomfort, adequate nutrition and no health loss. Award the existing 1-point, 6-round relief with its shared 12-round cooldown, using maximum rather than addition across shelter, mantle, exercise and fire. Repeated qualifying enjoyment remains eligible. Separately support maintained thermal refuge within that same source: after qualification, each continuing qualifying participation round raises a source-local sustained value by 0.025 to cap 1; other rounds decay it by 0.003 to zero. Re-entry requires three qualifying rounds; the short award retains its cooldown. Combine transient and sustained values by maximum, cap 1, and pass through existing mental accounting without modifying protected balances. Emit measured participation and source changes for replay. No reward for requesting, learning, building, lighting, ownership or merely remaining near an ineffective fire; health and survival remain independent.\",\n      \"visualReview\": \"The paid effect must be a persistent, spatially located hearth with actual cover, fuel, flame, embers and residue, not a warmth icon attached to Lin. Animation follows recorded combustion and weather; blocked heat and extinguished fires cannot look like active warming. Replay shows construction progress, ignition effort and failure, material payments, fuel depletion, cancellation and actual per-recipient temperature changes. A comfort indicator appears only after the measured event conditions qualify and must not imply safety or healing.\",\n      \"learning\": 6\n    }\n  ]\n}","logprobs":[]}
